reason: Reached only through electron-builder's Electron downloader (app-builder-lib -> @electron/get 3 -> got 11 -> cacheable-request). got creates its cacheable-request client only when a cache option is supplied; neither app-builder-lib nor this project's build configuration supplies one, so the max-stale code never runs. The package is build tooling, absent from the desktop app and the Docker image. Released 4.3.0 does not change max-stale handling, and overriding @electron/get to 5 under electron-builder 26 drops its download timeout, proxy agent and server-error retries. Revisit when a stable electron-builder release depends on @electron/get 5.

The reviewed advisory requires attacker-controlled numeric precision in a format string and has no published patched version. The only chain is electron-builder -> app-builder-lib -> @electron/get 3 -> global-agent 3 -> roarr 2 -> sprintf-js. Every global-agent logger format is a fixed string without numeric precision; network URLs, headers and errors enter structured context, never the format argument. Single-string roarr calls use the fixed %s format. All three packages are build-only and excluded from the application and Docker runtime. Their exact locked versions, integrities and sole dependents are checked so a changed logging caller invalidates this review. Revisit when the upstream advisory publishes a fix or the downloader removes this chain.
